title_vi: Các chiến lược bộ đệm hàng đầu

source_snapshot.note: Fetched the pinned commit from GitHub; git rev-parse of the path gives the source map's blob OID. Non-empty source body read; no source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Redis là bộ đệm dùng trong thử nghiệm của bài này.
Chiến lược đọc ghi là một mục trong bản đồ các câu hỏi khi dùng bộ đệm.
Write-behind mất dữ liệu khi bộ đệm không lưu xuống đĩa.

claims.evidence: Statements were checked against the Ehcache 3 Cache Usage Patterns page at ehcache/ehcache3 commit efea774551dcfdcfe54ec105dcfbfd70a42d8b6b and the Cache-Aside pattern page at MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036, read from partial clones, and against an experiment run on 2026-10-18 with Redis 7.0.15 (redis-py 8.1.0) as the cache and SQLite 3.45.1 (synchronous=FULL) as the system of record.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright 1.56, headless) rendered lesson.md converted by markdown-it (CommonMark, tables, raw HTML) with a 16 px page gutter and every <details> open, at 320, 375 and 430 px: document scrollWidth equalled the viewport at each width. Smallest figure text from the SVG font sizes times the shown scale: 13.5 px at 320, 15.0 px at 375. python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser measured every figure line. Not GitHub's renderer, not a real phone, not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: Cache-aside: application code reads the cache, on a miss reads the system of record, stores the value in the cache and returns it; read-through: the cache has a loader that reads the system of record on a miss.
claims.verified_by: Read; in the experiment 100 cache-aside reads of one key caused 1 database read.

claims.claim_vi: Write-through: the cache's writer stores the value in the system of record while updating the cache, the caller waiting; write-behind queues the write for later, letting the caller move on faster at the cost of lag before the system of record is updated.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment measured a median of about 1776 us per write-through write and about 382 us per write-behind write, and lost all 100 queued writes when the non-persistent Redis was killed before the flush.

claims.claim_vi: Cache-as-SoR combines read-through with write-through or write-behind; it keeps application code simpler and lets the cache solve the thundering-herd problem.
claims.verified_by: Read; not tested. The gloss of thundering herd is general knowledge.

claims.claim_vi: With cache-aside an application writes the data store and then invalidates the cache item; the pattern does not guarantee consistency; between a write and the next read a reader can see stale data; expiration should match the access pattern and not be too short.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment reproduced, step by step, a slow reader putting the old value 100 back after the writer set 120 and deleted the key, leaving the cache at 100 for its 300 s TTL.

claims.claim_vi: Write-around writes only the data store, so a cached copy stays old until it expires or is removed.
claims.verified_by: Source names the strategy only; behaviour shown in the experiment (database 130, cache still 120).

design_notes_vi: Hai thẻ đọc, ba thẻ ghi, bốn ghi chú kết quả thử. Giữ tên tiếng Anh của từng chiến lược vì đó là tên người học sẽ gặp; bài giải nghĩa bằng tiếng Việt. Vẽ bằng scripts/figures.
source_deviations: Source names the five strategies and leaves the details to its image, which is not used; the lesson explains each from the Ehcache and Microsoft documentation and tests what each one costs.
Lesson adds the stale-read interleaving of cache-aside and the loss of queued writes under write-behind, both reproduced in the experiment.

Lesson adds the common cache-aside write path (write the database, then delete the key) from the Microsoft pattern page, and the read-through plus write-through or write-behind combination from Ehcache.
